skill.name: skill-writer
skill.description: Guides users through creating Agent Skills for Claude Code, including scope, frontmatter, structure, validation, and troubleshooting.
skill.summary: Guides users through planning, writing, validating, and testing Claude Code Agent Skills.
skill.author: pytorch

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting and checklist text, not executable Ruby backticks or reconnaissance. One filesystem finding is confirmed because the skill instructs creating a hidden Claude Code skill directory under the user home, which can persist future agent behavior. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Ask for explicit user approval before creating or modifying files under ~/.claude/skills, and show the exact target path first.
Add guidance to review generated skills before use, prefer project-scoped skills for shared work, and set allowed-tools for limited workflows.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Agent Skill Authoring
semantic_findings.description: The skill guides creation of personal and project Agent Skills, including files under ~/.claude/skills. Generated skills can change future agent behavior, so creation should require clear user consent and review.

content.value_statement: Creating Agent Skills requires clear scope, valid frontmatter, and tested activation behavior. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users through a complete skill authoring workflow.
actual_capabilities: Guides users through choosing personal or project skill locations.
Explains required SKILL.md YAML frontmatter fields.
Shows standard folder structures for single-file and multi-file skills.
Provides description writing guidance for reliable skill discovery.
Includes validation and troubleshooting checklists for activation issues.
Recommends allowed-tools and progressive disclosure patterns.
limitations: It does not validate skills with an automated parser.
It does not provide a complete marketplace packaging workflow.
It may create files only when the active agent has filesystem access.
Generated skills still need user review before installation.

use_cases.title: Create a Personal Skill
use_cases.description: Build a focused skill for an individual workflow, with clear triggers and a valid SKILL.md file.

use_cases.title: Document Team Workflows
use_cases.description: Convert repeatable project practices into a project skill that teammates can inspect and share.

use_cases.title: Review Skill Quality
use_cases.description: Check a draft skill for naming, frontmatter, examples, dependencies, and activation clarity.

prompt_templates.title: Start a New Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a Claude Code Agent Skill for [workflow]. Ask me the key scope questions first.

prompt_templates.title: Write SKILL.md
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a SKILL.md for a skill named [skill-name]. It should help with [task] and activate when users mention [triggers].

prompt_templates.title: Add Supporting Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-file skill structure for [workflow]. Include what belongs in references, examples, scripts, and templates.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Activation Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this skill draft for discovery quality, frontmatter validity, scope creep, tool permissions, and testing gaps.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for reviewing pull requests in our repository.
output: A focused skill name and description for pull request review.
A SKILL.md outline with review steps and expected checks.
A validation checklist for testing activation and behavior.

output_examples.input: Improve this draft skill description so Claude Code finds it reliably.
output: A clearer description with concrete trigger phrases.
Notes about missing file types, operations, or context clues.
Suggested tests to confirm the skill activates correctly.

output_examples.input: Turn our deployment checklist into a project skill.
output: A project-scoped skill structure for the repository.
Step-by-step instructions for the deployment workflow.
Best practices for dependencies, permissions, and team review.

best_practices: Keep each skill focused on one capability with specific trigger phrases.
Use project skills for team workflows and personal skills for individual preferences.
Test activation with realistic user requests before relying on the skill.
anti_patterns: Do not create broad skills that combine unrelated workflows.
Do not use vague descriptions that omit file types, actions, or triggers.
Do not install generated skills without reviewing their instructions and tool permissions.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create Claude Code Agent Skills with valid frontmatter, clear instructions, examples, and validation steps.

faq.question: Can it create both personal and project skills?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when to use personal skills and when to place skills inside a project repository.

faq.question: Does it write production-ready skills automatically?
faq.answer: It can draft complete skill files, but users should review scope, permissions, dependencies, and examples before use.

faq.question: Does it support multi-file skills?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes optional reference files, examples, scripts, and templates for progressive disclosure.

faq.question: How does it improve skill discovery?
faq.answer: It teaches description patterns that include the task, trigger phrases, file types, and usage context.

faq.question: Is this only for Claude Code?
faq.answer: The instructions target Claude Code Agent Skills, but the planning guidance can help users of Claude and Codex.
